name: Our Lady of Victory Basilica
history: Father Nelson Baker, famous for his charities for orphans and the poor, unveiled plans for a shrine to Mary after a fire damaged the old church in 1916. Building began in 1921, the first Mass was held at Christmas 1925, and it was consecrated on 25 May 1926. Two months later Pius XI named it a basilica, only the second in the U.S.
arch: A marble Renaissance Revival church by Emile Ulrich with a great copper dome. After lightning damaged the marble towers in 1941, they were replaced by lower copper-domed towers.
features: It cost $3.2 million and was finished without the parish taking on any debt.
Its copper roof weathered green, like the Statue of Liberty.

look.d: The copper turned green with weathering, like the Statue of Liberty.
These copper-tipped towers replaced the marble ones damaged by lightning in 1941.

fun: Father Baker ran the basilica and its charities until his death in 1936.
journal: Father Baker's marble gift to Mary, paid for with no debt. Green dome by Lake Erie.
